building.title: Thomas Building, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 110's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, trimmed where its neighbours meet it (building.outline_note), in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). campus_outline: the campus.json ring as it is, kept for the record; the site replaces block 110 by its id. The campus map's second ring, the courtyard, is not in either.
building.outline_note: campus_outline with three trims, so that within frame.near_outline (1.5 m: the south-east face's returns stand 0.9-1.3 m outside the campus ring, the north-east's up to 0.9 m) no neighbour's returns count as 110's. (1) The Thomas Building Extension's link (110N's, as its config says): a notch in the north-east edge (vertices 9-13) where the link stands, in 110N's view frame (its frame.expected) from x -14.5 to 9.5 and back to z 21.9. In the LiDAR the link's glazed roof (16.7-17.2 m above 34.6) runs over 110's north-east parapet and ends at z 20.4 of that frame, where 110's flat roof at 15.8 begins; the notch is the link's x -13 to 8 and z to 20.4, widened by near_outline on each side. (2) Lippincott Cottage (118), 1.3 m off the north-west edge at the west corner: the corner (vertex 6) and the edge's first 9 m pulled in by 0.7 m (vertices 6-8). (3) The Overbridge (129), which lands on the round stair at the south-west end: the ring's stub where it lands and the vertex beside it (campus vertices 17-21) replaced by a cut 1.6 m back from the bridge's end, 1.6 m wider than it each side (vertices 23-24). With campus_outline the data stage took 28,362 building returns more than 3 m up, 341 of them the link's (110N's frame x -13..8, z 12..20.4), 25 the cottage's (within 0.6 m of its outline) and 41 the bridge's (within 0.6 m of its outline, past its end); with this ring it takes 27,940, none of theirs, and leaves out 15 of 110's own (the stair's wall beside the bridge and a few at the notch's corners).

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the point whose ground is the model's y = 0, where place.py meets the map's ground. The foot of the south-east face, the face to the road, near its middle, 0.6-0.9 m out from the wall, where the LiDAR's ground is 36.17 m (15 ground returns within 1 m: 35.96-36.25 for p10-p90): no door the photographs show stands on this face.

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline (building.outline_note: none of 110N's link, Lippincott Cottage's or the Overbridge's): centre = mean x/y of those higher than tower_above m, the roofs of the four ranges round the courtyard (14.3-19 m above the ground; a plant room at the east corner to 25 m); axis = the bearing of most of the walls seen from above (axis_from walls), of the two square to each other the one nearest the principal axis of all the building's points (spine_below 30 m, spine_radius 45 m: the whole building, 59 x 43 m, whose long axis runs south-west to north-east), pointing south-west (bearing -135.18 deg); toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: south-east (134.82 deg), to the road and the panoramas. The screening's spine (3 to 9.7 m within 30 m) took mostly the courtyard's low returns and gave the cross axis, with +z to the south-west, away from the road.

streetview.pano_ids_note: S_C8 (2024-08, 40 m from the centre, 17 m out from the face to the road) sees that face whole, a tree in front of its south-west end: the screening's sight-line test over the LiDAR gives its walls facing that way 86%; its 143 tiles were bought for this building on 2026-10-28. oWaF (2024-08, 55 m), bought for 110N on 2026-10-27, sees the north-east end and the east corner; the half of its views toward the face to the road needs 66 tiles never bought and is left black, which the sky masks take as ignored. MOQA, 110N's other panorama, sees 110 almost only behind 110N and is not pinned. Every one's copyright reads "From the Owner, Photo by: Google".
streetview.camera_fixes_note: [x, z, pitch, yaw, roll] (landmarks/README.md). S_C8 (round 1, 2026-10-28): x at its recorded place (no vertical edge of known u to fix it), z, pitch, yaw and roll fitted to the photograph's four horizontal edges in the wide view, the parapet's top against the sky and the three bands' tops over the windows, against the LiDAR's ledges 15.13, 11.12, 7.12 and 2.38 m, between the two piers it sees square (the panorama's stitching seams at about 720 and 1300 px shift a ledge by 10-25 px beyond them); cut again level by its roll, the middle's rms is about 2-3 px. oWaF: where the Thomas Building Extension's round 1 fixed it from its own photograph's edges (110N's config: [31.69, 12.34] in 110N's frame, 0.79 m from the recorded place, turned 2.21 deg left), moved into this frame through both configs' frame.expected (NZTM 238.996, 169.925): x and z, and the yaw, which is the panorama's heading and the same in any frame. Its pitch and roll are not carried over: 110N's views look 64 deg away from these, where a tilted panorama's roll and pitch differ, so they stay the cut's (0, and no roll).

compare.note: The Thomas Building Extension (110N, on the site since #122) stands between oWaF and this building's north-east end and the glazed link before it: the compare draws 110N's model as an occluder (viewer/mask.js: moved into this frame through both configs' frame.expected and ground), and the pixels where it hides this building count in neither the IoU nor the luma.
